title: await_sandbox_verdict is inert; only observable effect is a 30s stall
detail: Both angles independently found ITEM-3's readiness wait cannot change any verdict: the sweep skips every run_in_sandbox row before probing, and should_sandbox() requires run_in_sandbox, so no probed row consults sandbox state. The correctness angle MEASURED a 30.11s lib-test run caused entirely by SANDBOX_READY_TIMEOUT. I had seen 30.13s in my own earlier run and not questioned it.
resolution: Removed the wait, both consts, await_verdict_with and its three unit tests. The skip IS the ordering guarantee and is structural rather than timing-dependent, which is strictly stronger than a timed wait; the module doc now makes that argument explicitly. Measured: the boot_probe integration suite went from 32.62s to 2.52s.

title: TEST-1/TEST-6 'untested' assertion is satisfied by the column DEFAULT
detail: mcp_servers.last_health_check_status DEFAULTs to 'untested' and the create path writes no health record for a sandboxed row, so deleting the skip's record_health_check_on outright would still pass. The assertion could not distinguish 'recorded untested' from 'never touched the row' — the third vacuous-test finding on this workstream.
resolution: Both tests now seed a stale 'unhealthy' verdict + reason before the act, and additionally assert the stale reason was REPLACED and the new reason is non-empty. The assertion now proves a write.

title: not_testable computed independently of the branch actually taken
detail: not_testable was derived from existing.run_in_sandbox alone while the is_built_in arm is evaluated first, so a row that were both would have a genuine probe failure filed as 'untested'. Unreachable today (no built-in sets run_in_sandbox) but the guard and the branch encoded different predicates.
resolution: The flag is now SET BY the branch that runs (`not_testable = true` inside the sandboxed arm), so the two cannot diverge.

title: Doc comments orphaned by the auto-disable removal
detail: mcp/mod.rs spawn site still promised 'auto-disable unreachable ones'; events.rs named the boot check as an AutoDisabled emitter twice; connection_health.rs described 'list / record / disable' through the passed pool and 'a boot-time auto-disable is visible next time'.
resolution: All six sites rewritten to the actual post-change control flow.

title: Two functions' doc comments merged onto one
detail: The prose written for sandboxed_server_not_testable had no separator before health_record_for's own doc, so it attached to the wrong function and sandboxed_server_not_testable shipped undocumented.
resolution: Doc block moved onto the function it describes.

title: Test Connection is neutralised for a whole class, and the UI still paints it red
detail: sandboxed_server_not_testable keeps success:false, and BOTH UI call sites map success===false to message.error(). A user gets a red error toast whose own body reads 'This is a limit of the test, NOT a problem with the server.' I fixed the badge tooltips in DRIFT-1 and missed the toasts — the same defect one layer up. Verified by reading handleTest and handleSaveAndTest.
resolution: Both toast sites now branch on the row's own run_in_sandbox (already present client-side, so no public API field was added) and use message.info with the backend's explanation.

title: Sandbox guard bypassed when `existing` fails to resolve; health write was unscoped
detail: not_testable and the sandboxed arm key off `existing` (loaded via the ownership- and is_system=false-scoped lookup), but the health write used request.id unscoped. So POSTing a SYSTEM sandboxed row's id to the USER route resolves existing=None, probes on the host, and stamps that system row 'unhealthy' with the verbatim host-allowlist message — re-creating on the system row the exact badge and wording this change removes. The unscoped write pre-dates the diff; what is new is that INV-2 was claimed while holding only on the resolved path.
resolution: Both routes now gate the health write on the SCOPED lookup (`existing.as_ref().map(|s| s.id)`) rather than request.id.

title: Persisted-vocabulary contract in models.rs is now false; generated artifacts stale
detail: The doc said 'Defaults to untested for freshly-created rows that have never been probed' and 'reason: None on healthy / untested' — both false once a declined probe writes untested WITH a reason and a fresh timestamp. Those doc strings are the source of 8 locations across both workspaces' openapi.json + types.ts.
resolution: Source doc corrected, and all four generated artifacts patched to match. A full regen was attempted and REVERTED: this worktree's config has js_tool and voice disabled, so regenerating deleted 3,845 lines belonging to another worker's in-flight feature-surface reduction. The surgical patch was verified by the repo's own golden oracle (openapi::tests::types_ts_parity + _desktop), which was itself proven non-vacuous by introducing a one-word mismatch and observing it go RED.

title: New error code duplicates an existing one for the identical predicate
detail: SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE/400 was introduced for `get_state().is_none()`, which user_policy::enforce::require_sandbox_state already answers with MCP_SANDBOX_DISABLED/422. Two codes and two statuses for one condition, and 400 blames the client for a deployment-side absence.
resolution: Aligned to MCP_SANDBOX_DISABLED + unprocessable_entity. Free to do because the branch is new — nothing ever returned the other code.

title: Test registration broke the file's comment-after-mod convention
detail: The leading comment landed between `mod runtime;` and a pre-existing comment, retargeting that comment onto the new module.
resolution: Comment moved after the mod line, matching the file.

title: 'unhealthy' is now unreachable for sandboxed rows, and EVERY user stdio server is sandboxed
detail: Verified independently: user_policy/enforce.rs:56 and :85 force run_in_sandbox=Some(true) on every user stdio server, on create AND on every update. So the skip's blast radius is the whole user-stdio class, not just the Rscript case. All four health writers now skip or write 'untested' for that class, so no probe path can ever mark one unhealthy.
resolution: ACCEPTED, not fixed — and stated plainly in the PR rather than left implicit. Before this change that class did get a verdict, but it was a WRONG verdict produced by host-probing a guest-only command; removing a wrong signal is not removing a correct one. There is genuinely no probe path that can validate a sandboxed server today, and inventing one (a sandbox-capable Test Connection) is DEC-4's recorded follow-up. Escalated to the owner as the honest cost of the fix.

title: Auto-disable removal costs a re-dial per chat turn for genuinely dead non-sandboxed servers
detail: Tool collection iterates accessible servers in a sequential loop gated only on `enabled`. A permanently dead enabled server previously dropped out at the next restart; now it is re-dialled every chat request, and the stdio connect path has no handshake timeout (timeout_seconds is only honoured in client/http.rs).
resolution: ACCEPTED. The owner's brief explicitly required that 'a probe failure must not silently DISABLE an admin's server on boot', so ITEM-2 is a requested behaviour change, not an invention. The cost the auditor identifies is real and is now stated in the PR body and DEC-2 so the owner decides with it in view. The missing stdio handshake timeout is pre-existing and out of scope.

title: llm_repository solved this exact problem with a NEW status value, not by overloading 'untested'
detail: The sibling module added `unverified` with a CHECK-constraint migration, an API enum, and a distinct UI treatment, with the comment 'a state that is invisible in the UI is a state the operator reads as healthy'. This change overloads 'untested' and encodes the distinction only as 'reason is non-null', so the two meanings share a tag, tone, text and data-testid.
resolution: ACCEPTED as a follow-up, not adopted here. Matching it means a migration, a public enum, an OpenAPI regen for both workspaces and a UI treatment — which would also take the branch out of LIGHT tier. Recorded as the better long-term shape, with the precedent named so the follow-up does not have to rediscover it.

title: The two boot sweeps now behave oppositely for the same event
detail: llm_repository's boot sweep still calls disable_for_health_failure and documents itself as mirroring 'the MCP module's startup probe pattern'. After this change the same admin, on one restart, sees an unreachable LLM repository disabled and an unreachable MCP server not.
resolution: ACCEPTED, out of scope — changing another module's boot behaviour is a separate decision with its own review. Named in the PR body so the owner sees the divergence rather than discovering it, and so whoever resolves it does so deliberately in one direction.

title: Neither UI change has automated coverage
detail: The two tooltip branches and the two toast branches change behaviour with no spec touched; data-testid=mcp-health-untested appears nowhere under ui/tests.
resolution: ACCEPTED and stated rather than papered over. Covering it means an E2E that stands up a sandboxed stdio row, which needs a code_sandbox-enabled deployment and a rootfs — disproportionate here. Recorded in TESTS.md as a known coverage gap.

title: await_verdict_is_bounded_when_the_status_never_settles proved less than it claimed
detail: Timeout 150ms, assertion elapsed < 5s — an implementation ignoring the deadline entirely would pass.
resolution: Obsolete: the test was deleted with the mechanism it covered (F-1).

title: THE REPORTED BUG WAS STILL REPRODUCIBLE VERBATIM on the create-mode Enabled toggle
detail: Add system server -> stdio -> command Rscript -> tick Run in sandbox -> flip Enabled: red toast reading "Command 'Rscript' is not allowed on the host... Enable run-in-sandbox to use any command", and the switch snaps back off so the server is created disabled. Create mode sends no `id`, so `existing` is None and the new sandboxed branch cannot fire; build_ephemeral_server hardcodes run_in_sandbox:false so the new stdio branch cannot fire either. Round 1 saw this only as a 'related, lower' note and I filed it as a follow-up; the operator angle correctly rated it HIGH because it is the FIRST screen an admin meets.
resolution: Fixed client-side, where the intent is actually known: the create-mode toggle no longer probes a row the operator has marked sandboxed. That is agreement with the server, not a workaround — `enforce_on_create` skips the probe for such a row too, so any verdict gathered there is discarded on save. The toggle now enables in-form and says the server connects on the first real tool call.

title: Both reassuring messages asserted the server would connect without checking the sandbox exists
detail: On a deployment with code_sandbox.enabled:false, the badge promised 'connects on the first real tool call' and Test Connection said 'This is a limit of the test, NOT a problem with the server'. Both false: that row can never connect there, and the MCP page offered no way to find out. Corroborated by the security angle, which independently flagged the same class. Sharp detail from the auditor: my own first commit HAD wired init_status() in, and removing the inert wait removed the module's only sandbox-state awareness with it.
resolution: Added `sandbox_skip_reason()`, which consults `code_sandbox::config::init_status()` and says the sandbox is unavailable (naming the SandboxAvailability variant) when it is. Reinstates the awareness WITHOUT reinstating the wait.

title: enforce_on_create wrote no reason, so a fresh sandboxed row got the tooltip my own comment calls misleading
detail: The create skip returns without writing any health record, so the row sits at the column default 'untested' with reason NULL and the card falls back to 'Click Test Connection or toggle Enabled to run a probe' -- the two no-op actions. Every sandboxed row starts and stays in that state until a boot sweep or a manual test.
resolution: Both the create and enable skips now record 'untested' + sandbox_skip_reason(). This also gives F-21 its exit. Pinned by TEST-7, proven RED (`the create-time skip must record its reason; got None`).

title: Enabling a sandboxed server claimed a connection test passed while a red failure Alert was on screen for the same row
detail: The enable path calls persistServer(), which for a sandboxed row skips the probe -- yet the success toast read 'Server enabled - connection test passed' unconditionally, while the drawer rebound to a row still carrying the old unhealthy verdict and rendered 'Connection test failed at <date>'. Two contradictory statements about one row at the same instant.
resolution: The toast now only claims a test passed when one ran. Combined with F-19, the enable also records a true verdict, so the stale Alert clears rather than contradicting the toast.

title: The originally-reported row kept its false red badge after upgrade, with no discoverable remedy
detail: The owner's rcpa row is enabled=false + unhealthy. The boot sweep lists WHERE enabled = true, so it never touches it; toggling Enabled hit the skip and wrote nothing, so the badge stayed red still telling them to enable a flag the row already sets. Only Test Connection cleared it, which no operator would associate with 'clear a stale badge'.
resolution: Fixed as a consequence of F-19: the enable transition now records a true verdict, so the remedy an operator actually reaches for is the one that works.

title: The Enabled tooltip promised a probe that never runs, and contradicted the reason it appended
detail: Disabled sandboxed row: 'Click to enable (a connection test will run first)' -- none runs. Enabled sandboxed row: 'the server is reachable and queried by the LLM' followed, in the same hover, by a recorded reason saying reachability was never established.
resolution: A sandboxed row now gets its own baseline in both directions, asserting only what is true (offered to the LLM; click to enable).

title: The published field doc overstated the limitation -- and that text licensed the reassuring UI copy
detail: I had written 'no probe path can validate one, because every path probes on the host'. False: connection_health::probe passes the REAL server to run_connection_test, so it sandboxes whenever sandbox state exists. Only Test Connection is structurally host-only (its ephemeral server hardcodes the flag). My own error, published into 8 locations across both workspaces.
resolution: Corrected in source and in all four generated artifacts, re-verified by the types_ts_parity oracle.

title: One row explained itself two different ways depending on which path wrote last
detail: The boot skip and Test Connection wrote different prose into the same Untested tooltip, so the text flipped on every reboot after a manual test. Neither wrong; they read as two diagnoses of one row.
resolution: All four skip sites now share sandbox_skip_reason(), so there is one diagnosis.

title: Dead shared toast helper still encoded the behaviour just fixed away
detail: connectionTestToast.tsx still mapped success:false to message.error. Confirmed callerless, so not a live defect -- but a ready-made way to reintroduce the contradiction.
resolution: Given the same notTestable branch as the two live call sites.

title: Stale rationale left in run_startup_health_check's own doc
detail: 'a boot-time auto-disable is visible the next time the user opens the MCP servers list' -- there is no boot-time auto-disable any more.
resolution: Fixed. Root cause of it surviving round 1: my batch edit asserted on a later item and aborted BEFORE writing, so three earlier replacements in that batch were silently lost. Re-applied and verified by grep.

title: New error text disclosed the deployment config key and allowlist to any tool-invoking user
detail: The MCP_SANDBOX_DISABLED message named `code_sandbox.enabled: true` and the host allowlist, and bypassed errors::upstream_error, which exists to log the leaky detail and return a stable message. A regular user invoking a tool on a group-assigned sandboxed server would learn the deployment's config state.
resolution: Reworded to keep the actionable correction (the sandbox is unavailable; the allowlist is not the constraint) while dropping the literal config key and the allowlist enumeration.

title: WIN: the F-7 fix closes a real PRE-EXISTING cross-tenant write
detail: Not a defect in the branch -- the security angle established that the change I made for consistency is a security fix. On origin/main, record_health_check is `UPDATE mcp_servers ... WHERE id = $1` with NO ownership predicate, and both handlers called it with the unscoped request.id. So any holder of mcp_servers::create could stamp last_health_check_status='unhealthy' plus a reason onto ANY row in the table -- another user's personal server, or a system server. Gating the write on the scoped lookup closes it on both routes, symmetrically, and introduces no existence oracle.
resolution: Closed. Recorded here because it must be called out in the PR body: it is the most consequential thing in the branch and I had filed it merely as an inconsistency.

title: PRE-EXISTING: Test Connection bypasses the policy that forces user stdio servers into the sandbox (host RCE)
detail: build_ephemeral_server hardcodes run_in_sandbox:false and never calls the policy enforcer, so any holder of mcp_servers::create can POST an id-less test-connection with command npx and args [attacker-package]; resolve_command rewrites npx to `bun x` and args append verbatim, executing attacker code on the HOST outside the sandbox user_policy mandates. Independently rediscovered here by a second auditor on a second branch -- I escalated the same finding on PR #16.
resolution: NOT fixed here and out of scope. The branch NARROWS it (a stored sandboxed row now short-circuits before any spawn); the id-less path remains. Re-escalated in the PR body with the note that two independent audits have now found it.

title: PRE-EXISTING: on a sandbox-off deployment a user cannot even turn their own stdio server OFF
detail: enforce_on_user_transport_change calls require_sandbox_state() before anything else, so every PUT returns 422 MCP_SANDBOX_DISABLED -- including the minimal {enabled:false} the drawer sends. The only exit is Delete, which discards the configuration. Findings F-18/F-19 make such a row look benign while it is both broken and un-editable.
resolution: NOT fixed -- pre-existing and in another module's enforcement order. Escalated: it is the direct answer to 'a state the operator cannot get out of', and it interacts with this change.

title: PRE-EXISTING: a sandboxed row whose command IS host-allowed silently runs unsandboxed
detail: should_sandbox() is stdio && run_in_sandbox && get_state().is_some(). With the sandbox absent, a row with run_in_sandbox:true and command npx/python3/node falls to connect_native and spawns on the host with NO error and no badge change -- the new MCP_SANDBOX_DISABLED arm only fires inside the allowlist REJECTION branch. Since user policy force-sandboxes every user stdio server, this is the common shape.
resolution: NOT fixed. The branch amplifies visibility of it (the sweep no longer probes such a row), which is why it is escalated rather than left silent. A correct fix is to refuse the host fallback for a run_in_sandbox row outright, which changes runtime behaviour for existing deployments and needs the owner's decision.
